unit: Ch 9: Special Features of Audit of Different Type of Entities
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Government Audit - Background & Legal Framework
explain: Government audit ensures executive accountability to Parliament regarding public revenue and spending.
Parliament controls expenditure through demand for grants funded via the Consolidated Fund of India or States.
Consolidated Fund includes tax revenues, loans taken, and loan repayments received by the Government.
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) scrutinises Appropriation Accounts after spending takes place.
The Comptroller & Auditor General (C&AG) is appointed by the President of India and functions independently.
C&AG removal requires a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting in each House of Parliament on grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity.
Article 149 defines C&AG duties and powers; Article 150 prescribes accounting forms on C&AG advice; Article 151 mandates submitting audit reports to the President/Governor.

flow.title: Parliamentary Control & Audit Workflow
steps: Parliament votes on Demand for Grants
Funds released from Consolidated Fund
Executive incurs expenditure
Appropriation Accounts prepared
C&AG conducts statutory audit
Reports submitted under Article 151
Public Accounts Committee scrutinises report

topics.example: When a Ministry plans a national highway project, funds are voted by Parliament from the Consolidated Fund, spent by the ministry, and later audited by C&AG to ensure proper authorization.
remember: Consolidated Fund of India is established under Article 266.
Removal of C&AG requires a 2/3rd majority in both Houses of Parliament.
Article 151 mandates laying C&AG reports before Parliament/State Legislatures.
mistakes: Confusing Article 150 (form of accounts prescribed by President on C&AG advice) with Article 151 (submission of C&AG reports).

quiz.q: Under which Article of the Constitution are C&AG reports submitted to the President or Governor?
o: Article 149
Article 150
Article 151
Article 266
quiz.why: Article 151 requires C&AG reports to be submitted to the President or Governor to be laid before the Legislature.

quiz.q: What majority is required in Parliament to remove the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
o: Simple majority of total members
2/3rd majority of members present and voting
3/4th majority of total members
Executive order of the President alone
quiz.why: C&AG can only be removed like a Supreme Court Judge by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting in each House.

topics.title: Comptroller and Auditor General (C&AG) - Duties & Powers
topics.section: C&AG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
explain: C&AG compiles and submits accounts of the Union and States from initial accounts rendered by treasuries.
Audits all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, and Public Accounts of Union and States.
Audits receipts and expenditure of bodies substantially financed by grants/loans from the Consolidated Fund.
Substantially financed means grant/loan is at least ₹25 Lakhs AND not less than 75% of the body's total expenditure.
Scrutinises procedures for granting loans/grants for specific purposes to external non-foreign bodies.
Has the power to inspect any accounts office, inspect books/documents at specified places, ask questions, and dispense with detailed checks in favor of test checks.

flow.title: Substantially Financed Verification Test
steps: Identify total grant/loan from Consolidated Fund
Check if amount is >= ₹25 Lakhs
Check if amount is >= 75% of total expenditure
If both conditions met, entity is substantially financed
C&AG audits all receipts and expenditure of the body

topics.example: A social welfare trust receives a ₹30 Lakh grant from the Government, which makes up 80% of its total budget. Since it exceeds ₹25 Lakhs and 75% of total spending, C&AG can audit its accounts.
remember: Substantially financed threshold: Grant/Loan >= ₹25 Lakhs AND >= 75% of total expenditure.
C&AG Act 1971 governs duties, powers, and service conditions.
mistakes: Assuming C&AG can inspect books without notice; reasonable previous notice must be given for inspecting books of grant-receiving bodies.

quiz.q: An entity receives a grant of ₹30 Lakhs, which constitutes 70% of its total expenditure. Is it considered substantially financed under the C&AG Act?
o: Yes, because the grant exceeds ₹25 Lakhs
No, because the grant is less than 75% of total expenditure
Yes, because both limits are independent
No, because the grant must exceed ₹50 Lakhs
quiz.why: To be substantially financed, the grant must be AT LEAST ₹25 Lakhs AND AT LEAST 75% of total expenditure.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a power of C&AG under the 1971 Act?
o: Inspect any accounts office under Government control
Dispense with detailed audit of any class of transactions
Modify the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013
Call for books and documents to be sent to specified places
quiz.why: C&AG has powers of inspection, document requisition, and test checks, but cannot modify statutory Acts of Parliament.

topics.title: Expenditure Audit - Types & Propriety Principles
explain: Audit against Rules & Orders ensures spending conforms to statutory rules, regulations, and financial codes.
Audit of Sanctions ensures every expenditure item has a general or special sanction from a competent authority.
Audit against Provision of Funds verifies that expenditure matches allocated budget grants and stays within limits.
Propriety Audit evaluates wisdom, economy, and faithfulness of spending beyond formal rule compliance.

Propriety principles: Spending should not exceed occasion demands; no self-benefit sanctions; public funds not used for private benefit unless custom/court order applies; allowances not a source of profit.
Performance Audit (3 Es) evaluates Efficiency (output vs input ratio), Economy (acquiring resources cheaply), and Effectiveness (achieving targeted goals).

flow.title: Five Pillars of Government Expenditure Audit
steps: Audit against Rules & Orders
Audit of Sanctions
Audit against Provision of Funds
Propriety Audit (Moral/Wisdom check)
Performance Audit (Efficiency, Economy, Effectiveness)

topics.example: Constructing a modern telephone exchange building that remains unused for 5 years satisfies regularity rules, but fails Propriety Audit as wasteful/avoidable expenditure.
remember: Performance Audit assesses the 'Three Es': Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness.
Propriety Audit goes beyond rule compliance to examine financial morality and common sense.
mistakes: Believing C&AG has final authority to interpret Constitution/laws; final legal interpretation rests with courts.

quiz.q: Evaluating whether a government scheme achieved its targeted social outcome is part of which audit?
o: Audit against Rules & Orders
Audit of Sanctions
Effectiveness Audit (Performance Audit)
Audit against Provision of Funds
quiz.why: Effectiveness audit evaluates performance with reference to overall targeted objectives.

quiz.q: Which principle of Propriety Audit is violated if an officer sanctions an official travel allowance that yields a net profit to himself?
o: Allowances should not be a source of profit to recipients
Expenditure should conform to rules and orders
Provision of funds must exist in the budget
Sanctions must be issued by a higher authority
quiz.why: Propriety principles mandate that travelling allowances must be regulated so they do not become a source of profit.

topics.title: Audit of Receipts, Stores & Commercial Accounts
explain: Audit of Receipts ensures dues to government are correctly assessed, collected, and credited, with system checks against fraud.
Audit of Stores & Inventories verifies purchasing rules, reasonable prices, physical stocks, and avoids idle inventory.
Public commercial enterprises fall into Departmental Concerns, Statutory Corporations, and Government Companies.
Under Section 143(5), C&AG appoints statutory auditors for Government Companies and gives directions on audit scope.
Under Section 143(6), C&AG can conduct a Supplementary Audit within 60 days of receiving the audit report and comment upon it.
Under Section 143(7), C&AG has the power to order a Test Audit of government company accounts.

flow.title: C&AG Role in Government Company Audit
steps: C&AG appoints Statutory Auditor u/s 143(5)
C&AG issues directions for audit
Statutory Auditor submits report to C&AG
C&AG has 60 days for Supplementary Audit u/s 143(6)
C&AG issues comments/supplement to report
Comments placed before AGM and members

topics.example: If a government-owned power corporation is audited by a CA firm, C&AG can conduct a supplementary audit within 60 days and issue comments that must be sent to all shareholders.
remember: C&AG supplementary audit timeframe: within 60 days of receiving the statutory audit report.
Section 143(5) governs appointment of auditors in Government Companies.
mistakes: Thinking the Board of Directors of a Government Company appoints its statutory auditor; appointment is made by C&AG.

quiz.q: Within how many days from the receipt of the audit report can C&AG conduct a supplementary audit of a Government Company?
o: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days
quiz.why: Section 143(6) grants C&AG the right to conduct a supplementary audit within 60 days of receipt of the audit report.

quiz.q: Who appoints the statutory auditor of a Government Company registered under Companies Act, 2013?
o: Shareholders at AGM
Board of Directors
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
quiz.why: Section 143(5) empowers C&AG to appoint statutory auditors for Government Companies.

topics.title: Audit of Local Bodies (Municipalities)
topics.section: Local Fund Audit Wing / Municipal Acts
explain: Urban local authorities include Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, Notified Area Committees, Town Area Committees, and Cantonment Committees.
Revenue sources: Property taxes, octroi, profession tax, tolls, non-tax fees, and state grants (General purpose, Specific purpose, Statutory/Compensatory).
Budgetary formats lack strict separation of revenue/capital items; capital items are grouped under 'Extraordinary items'.
Audit is conducted by the State Government's Local Fund Audit Wing (though major corporations like Delhi/Mumbai can appoint external auditors).
Audit objectives: Fair presentation of financial statements, internal control evaluation, legal compliance, detecting fraud/errors, and Value for Money (3 Es).
Audit can surcharge local authority office-bearers for ultra vires (unauthorized/illegal) expenditure.

flow.title: Local Body Expenditure & Audit Mechanics
steps: State Government/Local Body raises revenue & receives grants
Budget passed with 'Extraordinary items' for capital spends
Executive incurs municipal expenditure
Local Fund Audit Wing / Auditor inspects accounts
Check for ultra vires actions & potential surcharge
Value for Money audit report issued

topics.example: If a city council spends municipal funds on a banquet outside its legal mandate, the auditor can flag the expense as ultra vires and initiate a surcharge on responsible officials.
remember: Municipal capital spending is classified under 'Extraordinary items' in budget formats.
State Local Fund Audit Wing usually audits municipal accounts.
mistakes: Assuming central government directly audits all municipal bodies; local bodies are created by state legislation and audited via state Local Fund wings.

quiz.q: Which category of grant compensates a local body for loss of revenue when the state government takes over a local tax?
o: General purpose grant
Specific purpose grant
Statutory and compensatory grant
Discretionary capital grant
quiz.why: Statutory and compensatory grants are provided by law to compensate for revenue lost due to state takeover of taxes.

quiz.q: An unauthorized expenditure beyond the legal powers of a municipal council can result in which audit action?
o: Disclaimer of opinion only
Surcharge on responsible personnel
Immediate dissolution of municipality
Refusal to issue audit report
quiz.why: Expenditure beyond legal powers (ultra vires) can lead to a 'surcharge' where individuals must personally reimburse the loss.

topics.title: Audit of Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs)
topics.section: Societies Act 1860 / Trusts Act 1882 / Companies Act 2013 Sec 8 / FCRA 2010
explain: NGOs can be formed as Societies, Trusts, or Section 8 Companies. Registration is required under FCRA 2010 for foreign funds and Income Tax Act for tax exemptions.
Section 8 companies must maintain accounts on an accrual basis u/s 128; non-Section 8 NGOs may follow cash or accrual basis.
Corpus contributions are capital receipts shown as liabilities in the Balance Sheet; Section 11(1)(d) of IT Act excludes corpus donations from total income.
Revolving funds are temporary loans rotated to beneficiaries; interest earned is added back or credited to Income & Expenditure.
Auditors of Section 8 NGOs are appointed by members; Trusts/Societies auditors are appointed by Management.
FCRA 2010 requires annual audit reports to be submitted to the Ministry of Home Affairs within 60 days of fiscal year end (by May 30).

flow.title: NGO Audit Planning Sequence
steps: Understand NGO mission, vision, and operational environment
Verify legal constitution (Trust Deed, MOA/AOA, Registration)
Check FCRA 2010, Income Tax 12A/80G compliances
Evaluate internal control, cash/digital receipts & grant agreements
Vouch corpus, earmarked, and revolving funds
Verify project expenditure & submit statutory reports (e.g. FCRA by May 30)

topics.example: An NGO receives $50,000 from a US donor. The auditor must verify it was deposited into a dedicated FCRA bank account and filed with the Ministry of Home Affairs by May 30.
remember: FCRA return deadline: Within 60 days of year-end (by May 30).
Section 8 NGOs MUST use accrual accounting.
Corpus contributions are capital receipts shown on the liabilities side.
mistakes: Believing non-Section 8 NGOs must use accrual accounting; they are permitted to use cash basis unless restricted by specific laws.

quiz.q: Under FCRA 2010, by what date must an NGO furnish its audited financial report for foreign contributions to the Ministry of Home Affairs?
o: March 31
May 30
September 30
December 31
quiz.why: FCRA 2010 requires reporting within 60 days of financial year end, which is May 30.

quiz.q: How should a voluntary donation received with a specific direction to form part of the NGO's permanent fund be treated?
o: Revenue income in Income & Expenditure Account
Corpus contribution shown as a liability in Balance Sheet
Deferred revenue expenditure
Operating receipt under cash flow
quiz.why: Donations towards corpus are capital receipts recorded as liabilities on the Balance Sheet.

topics.title: Audit of Sole Trader and Partnership Firm
explain: Sole traders have no statutory legal mandate for audit, but may get audited for bank loans or regulatory reasons.
Sole proprietor determines audit scope; contract should be in writing/engagement letter to prevent misunderstandings.
Partnership audit is agreed among partners or mandated by partnership deed; remuneration fixed by partners.
Incoming auditor of a sole trader or firm must communicate with the previous auditor.
Matters checked before starting partnership audit: firm name, duration, capital contributions, profit sharing ratio, interest on capital/drawings, borrowing powers, and partner salaries.
Advantages of firm audit: Settles disputes, facilitates valuation on dissolution/retirement/admission, reliable for bank financing, safeguard for non-working partners.

flow.title: Pre-Audit Process for Partnership Firm
steps: Receive written appointment letter signed by authorized partner
Communicate with previous auditor
Examine Partnership Deed & Minute books
Note profit sharing, interest, borrowing & salary rules
Perform verification of Profit & Loss and Balance Sheet
Report non-compliances with ICAI Accounting Standards

topics.example: Before auditing ABC & Co., the auditor reads the partnership deed to verify if Partner A is legally entitled to a 12% interest on capital and ₹20,000 monthly salary.
remember: Audit of sole trader and standard partnership firm is non-statutory unless mandated by tax law (e.g. Tax Audit).
Engagement letter must clearly define scope and limitations.
mistakes: Failing to communicate with the previous auditor when taking up a sole trader or partnership audit.

quiz.q: Why is a written engagement letter especially crucial in the audit of a sole proprietorship?
o: Because Companies Act mandates it
To clearly define scope and limitations since audit is non-statutory
To file it with the Registrar of Companies
To automatically grant tax exemption to the proprietor
quiz.why: Since sole trader audit is contractual, a written letter avoids scope misunderstandings.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of auditing a partnership firm?
o: Mitigates dispute possibilities among partners
Provides reliable evidence on retirement/death of a partner
Converts the firm into a limited liability company automatically
Safeguards interests of non-active partners
quiz.why: Audit improves reliability and trust but does not alter the legal constitution or liability structure of a firm.

topics.title: Audit of Limited Liability Partnerships (LLP)
topics.section: LLP Act 2008 / Rule 24 of LLP Rules 2009
explain: LLP combines features of company and partnership; minimum 2 partners, at least 2 Designated Partners holding DPIN.
Small LLP thresholds: Contribution <= ₹25 Lakhs (can be raised up to ₹5 Crore) AND Turnover <= ₹40 Lakhs (can be raised up to ₹50 Crore).
Exemption from audit: LLP whose turnover <= ₹40 Lakhs AND contribution <= ₹25 Lakhs is NOT required to audit accounts unless partners decide otherwise.
Books required: Cash receipts/expenditure, assets/liabilities, manufacturing/cost/inventory details, and other partner-decided items.
Statutory filings: Annual Return in Form 11 within 60 days of FY end; Statement of Account & Solvency in Form 8 within 30 days of 6 months after FY end.
Auditor appointment: Designated partners appoint auditor (1st year anytime before FY end; subsequent years at least 30 days before FY end; casual vacancies). If DP fails, partners appoint.

flow.title: LLP Audit Applicability & Filing Timeline
steps: Check Contribution (Limit: ₹25 Lakhs) & Turnover (Limit: ₹40 Lakhs)
If BOTH within limits -> Audit is OPTIONAL
If EITHER exceeds limit -> Mandatory Statutory Audit
File Form 11 (Annual Return) within 60 days of FY end with ROC
File Form 8 (Account & Solvency) within 30 days of 6 months post FY end

topics.example: An LLP has ₹20 Lakhs capital contribution and ₹50 Lakhs turnover. Because turnover exceeds ₹40 Lakhs, it MUST get its accounts audited under Rule 24.
remember: Small LLP audit exemption limits: Contribution <= ₹25 Lakhs AND Turnover <= ₹40 Lakhs.
Form 11: Annual return due within 60 days of FY end.
Form 8: Statement of Account & Solvency due within 30 days after 6 months from FY end.
mistakes: Thinking an LLP is exempt if ONLY ONE threshold is met; BOTH contribution and turnover must be within exemption limits to avoid mandatory audit.

quiz.q: An LLP has a capital contribution of ₹15 Lakhs and a turnover of ₹35 Lakhs. Is it mandatorily required to be audited?
o: Yes, all LLPs must be audited
No, because contribution <= ₹25 Lakhs and turnover <= ₹40 Lakhs
Yes, because turnover exceeds ₹25 Lakhs
No, only if it is registered as a public company
quiz.why: Both parameters are within exemption limits (Contribution <= 25L and Turnover <= 40L), so audit is optional.

quiz.q: What is the deadline for filing Form 8 (Statement of Account and Solvency) with ROC for an LLP?
o: Within 60 days of financial year end
Within 30 days from the end of 6 months of financial year
Within 90 days of AGM
By May 30 every year
quiz.why: Form 8 must be filed within 30 days from the end of six months of the financial year (i.e. Oct 30).

topics.title: Audit of Charitable Institutions
topics.section: Trust Deed / Public Trust Acts / Income Tax Act 1961
explain: Auditor must examine constitution, trust deed, and compliance with laws governing charitable trusts.
Verify internal checks over box collections, flag days, receipt books, counterfoils, and printed subscription lists.
Digital receipts (UPI, Cards, Gateways): Reconcile bank statements, gateway settlement reports, and donor software; check transaction fees, refunds, and access controls.
Vouch Legacies with correspondence; Grants with memo/certificates from officials.
Vouch Investment Income (dividend/interest warrants) and verify ex-dividend/cum-dividend purchases.
Inspect Rent rolls and tenancy agreements; check Income Tax Refunds (deducted at source) as charities are tax-exempt.
Vouch Grants Paid: Ensure spending aligns strictly with charitable objects and no trustee/managing committee member benefits directly or indirectly.

flow.title: Digital Donation Audit Procedure
steps: Extract digital receipt report from donor portal/software
Reconcile with payment gateway settlement reports
Match gross collections against actual bank credits
Verify gateway charges & MDR deductions in books
Check authorization for failed transactions, refunds, chargebacks
Test system interface & user access controls

topics.example: When auditing online donations to a relief trust, the auditor reconciles ₹10 Lakhs in UPI gateway logs with ₹9.9 Lakhs credited in bank statements, accounting for ₹10,000 in gateway fees.
remember: Charitable grant payments must NOT benefit any trustee or managing member directly or indirectly.
Tax deducted at source on investments must be claimed back as refund due to exemption.
mistakes: Overlooking gateway charges deducted before net settlement, which leads to understatement of both donation income and bank charges.

quiz.q: While auditing grants paid by a charitable institution, what critical restriction must the auditor verify?
o: Grants must only be paid in cash
No trustee or committee member benefits directly or indirectly from the grant
Grants must equal 100% of annual receipts
Grants require prior approval from C&AG
quiz.why: Auditor must ensure spending is strictly for charitable objects and no insider benefits from it.

quiz.q: Why should an auditor check TDS deducted on interest income earned by a charitable trust?
o: To pay additional income tax
To ensure refund is claimed, as eligible charities are tax-exempt
To transfer TDS to the corpus fund
To report non-compliance to C&AG
quiz.why: Exempt charitable trusts are entitled to a full refund of tax deducted at source on investment returns.

topics.title: Audit of Educational Institutions
topics.section: Trust Deed / University Acts / State Education Rules
explain: General: Examine Trust Deed/Regulations or Legislative Act; check Managing Committee minutes for bank operations and expense sanctions.
Fee verification: Reconcile Students Fee Register with Class Registers; vouch cash/digital collections (UPI, cards, Net Banking) against bank statements and Student Information System (SIS)/ERP.
Concessions & Fines: Verify free studentships/concessions against rules and authorized sanctions; check late fee fines or authorized remissions.
Admission Fees: Verify with admission slips; ensure credited to Capital Fund unless decided otherwise.
Caution Money: Confirm student caution deposits are shown as liabilities in the Balance Sheet, not transferred to revenue unless non-refundable.
Expenditure & Staff: Vouch capital spending with minute book; verify Provident Fund investments; check salary increases and budget variations.
Endowment Funds: Confirm prize endowment investments are segregated and excess interest is accumulated with corpus.

flow.title: Student Fee Audit Trail
steps: Compare Class Register (students on roll) with Fee Register
Check fee demand raised for each student
Vouch receipts (cash counterfoils & digital gateway reports)
Reconcile collections with SIS/ERP and Bank Statements
Verify arrears written off or carried forward
Confirm admission fee credited to Capital Fund

topics.example: A student pays ₹50,000 tuition fee via credit card. The auditor traces this from the college portal to the bank settlement statement and ensures it is correctly updated in the Students Fee Register.
remember: Caution Money must be reflected as a liability until refunded or legally forfeited.
Admission fees are credited to Capital Fund unless committee decides otherwise.
mistakes: Treating refundable caution money deposits as school income in the Profit & Loss statement.

quiz.q: How should refundable caution money collected from students at the time of admission be shown in financial statements?
o: As direct fee revenue in Income & Expenditure
As a liability in the Balance Sheet
As a reduction from establishment expenses
Credited directly to General Reserve
quiz.why: Caution money is refundable to students and must be shown as a liability until repaid or forfeited.

quiz.q: What procedure should an auditor perform regarding fee concessions granted to students?
o: Verify concessions against sanction of an authorized person as per rules
Automatically write off all concession amounts as bad debts
Capitalize fee concessions under fixed assets
Report concessions directly to the State Governor
quiz.why: The auditor must ensure concessions are granted strictly by authorized officials per managing committee rules.

topics.title: Audit of Hospitals
explain: Register of Patients: Vouch patient register with copy bills; verify selected period bills against attendance records.
Cash & Digital Collections: Check cash receipts; reconcile daily collections in Hospital Management Information System (HMIS)/billing software with bank settlement reports (UPI, Cards, Gateways).
Digital Audits: Verify MDR charges, convenience fees, patient refunds authorization, cancelled bills/chargebacks, and year-end cut-off for pending bank credits.
System Interface: Verify interface controls between HMIS, billing software, and financial ledger to prevent unauthorized data tampering.
Legacies & Grants: Ensure specific purpose donations/grants are properly applied and TDS refunds are claimed.
Inventories & Internal Check: Test internal check on receipt/issue of medicines, stores, linen, surgical tools; verify stock levels physically.
Depreciation: Ensure adequate depreciation is written off on medical apparatus and equipment.

flow.title: Hospital Revenue & Inventory Audit Flow
steps: HMIS records patient admission, doctor fee, lab tests, medicines
Billing software auto-generates patient invoice
Patient pays via cash/digital mode (UPI/Card)
Reconcile daily HMIS billing with bank credits & gateway reports
Verify internal check over medicine store receipts and issues
Perform physical stock verification of medicines & surgical supplies

topics.example: A patient is billed ₹50,000 for surgery. HMIS auto-transfers billing data to accounting software. The auditor checks that digital receipt reconciles with bank statements minus MDR fees.
remember: HMIS-to-Accounting software interface controls must prevent unauthorized alteration of billing data.
Audit must verify strict internal controls over expensive medicine store issues.
mistakes: Failing to reconcile year-end digital collections received before March 31 but credited by payment gateways in April.

quiz.q: Which of the following procedures is vital for auditing digital billing in a modern hospital?
o: Relying solely on paper receipts signed by doctors
Reconciling HMIS billing software records with bank/gateway settlement reports
Ignoring Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) deductions
Disregarding patient attendance registers
quiz.why: Auditing requires verifying interface reliability between HMIS, billing systems, and bank settlement statements.

quiz.q: How should internal control over hospital pharmacy stores be verified by the auditor?
o: Ensure medicines are issued only against proper doctor authorization and logged in inventory registers
Write off total medicine stock at year end automatically
Allow pharmacy staff to issue stores without records
Verify pharmacy bills only once every 5 years
quiz.why: Strong internal control requires proper authorization and recording for all receipts and issues of medicines.

topics.title: Audit of Clubs
explain: Entrance Fees: Vouch with member applications, counterfoil receipts, and Managing Committee minutes.
Subscriptions: Vouch with receipt counterfoils; reconcile total subscriptions due vs collected vs outstanding in Member Register.
Digital Subscriptions: Reconcile Club Management System with bank credits; check gateway charges, member portal access controls, and audit trails.
Member Dues & Arrears: Check cross-totals of Register of Members; verify recovery steps for arrears; report irrecoverable dues in Audit Report.
Foodstuffs & Bar Pricing: Test internal checks on charges for food, drinks, and special amenities (billiards, tennis); verify gross profit margins on bar/catering sales.
Inventories & Purchases: Vouch purchases of sports items, crockery, furniture; physically test stock of unsold provisions/stores at year end.
Management Powers: Check financial powers of Secretary; report cases where powers were exceeded for committee ratification.

flow.title: Club Subscription Audit Procedure
steps: Check Register of Members for active membership count
Calculate total subscription revenue due for the year
Vouch collections from bank/gateway reports & receipt counterfoils
Reconcile receipts with Club Management Software
Adjust opening arrears, advance subscriptions, and closing arrears
Flag irrecoverable member dues for audit report disclosure

topics.example: A club charges ₹12,000 annual subscription per member. The auditor checks 500 members = ₹60 Lakhs due, reconciles ₹55 Lakhs collected online, ₹3 Lakhs advance, and ₹2 Lakhs arrears.
remember: Irrecoverable member dues must be specifically mentioned in the Audit Report.
Verify gross profit margins earned on sale of foodstuffs, wines, and cigars.
mistakes: Not adjusting advance subscriptions received for the next financial year from current year revenue.

quiz.q: Where an auditor finds member subscription dues that are completely irrecoverable, what is the required reporting step?
o: Hide the amount under general expenses
Mention the irrecoverable dues specifically in the Audit Report
Surcharge the Club Secretary personally
Cancel the club's registration
quiz.why: Club audit rules require irrecoverable dues to be explicitly highlighted in the Audit Report.

quiz.q: Vouching purchases of sports equipment and crockery in a club involves tracing entries into which record?
o: Students Fee Register
Respective Inventory Registers
Rent Roll
FCRA Bank Account
quiz.why: Purchases of capital/asset items like sports goods and crockery must be traced to inventory registers.

topics.title: Audit of Cinema Halls / Multiplexes
topics.section: Cinematograph Acts / State Entertainment Tax Rules
explain: Internal Controls: Printed serially-numbered tickets; separate ticket series for different shows, classes, and advance bookings; ticket inventory in safe custody.
Daily Reconciliation: Verify end-of-show statement of tickets sold with cash collected; verify free passes record issued under proper authority.
Tax & Cash Book: Reconcile Entertainment/GST Tax collected with tickets issued; test-check Daily Statements with Cash Book entries.
Slide Ads & Restaurant: Verify slide/short ad charges with Slide Register and advertiser contracts; check restaurant income share (fixed sum or % of takings).
Film Hire Contracts: Vouch distributor payments with bills/agreements; examine unadjusted distributor advances for recoverability and write-off needs.
Digital & POS Controls: Verify online booking platforms (web/apps), QR code admission gate scanners (prevent duplicate scans), POS systems, convenience fees, and system audit trails.

flow.title: Multiplex Ticket Revenue Audit Cycle
steps: Track ticket sales from POS/website/third-party platforms
Verify QR code gate scanning validation reports
Agree daily show statements with payment gateway credits
Reconcile tax collected with total tickets issued per class
Vouch distributor film hire percentage against agreements
Check distributor advance balance recoverability

topics.example: A multiplex contracts a 40% box-office revenue share with a film distributor. The auditor checks daily ticket collection logs against distributor settlement bills to verify exact payout.
remember: No part of routine advertisement/repairs expenditure should be capitalized.
Unadjusted advances to film distributors must be assessed for recoverability.
mistakes: Capitalizing routine repair and promotional expenditure incurred for movie releases.

quiz.q: What should an auditor do regarding unadjusted advances paid to film distributors for movies that have already completed their run?
o: Treat them as permanent fixed assets
Inquire why advances were not adjusted and ensure provision is made if irrecoverable
Automatically credit them to restaurant revenue
Report them to the Local Fund Audit Wing
quiz.why: Advances for movies already screened should have been settled; if unrecoverable, a provision is required.

quiz.q: Scanning of QR codes at cinema entry gates is verified by auditors primarily to check which control?
o: That each ticket is validated only once and scanned count matches sold tickets
That food prices are discounted
That distributor payments are waived
That entertainment tax is exempted
quiz.why: QR code checks ensure gate entry control, preventing duplicate scans, unauthorized entry, or fake tickets.

topics.title: Audit of Hire Purchase and Leasing Companies
explain: Hire Purchase: Agreement where hirer gets possession and option to buy; ownership transfers on payment of LAST instalment; hirer can terminate anytime before.
Auditor checks for HP: Agreement in writing signed by all parties; explicit HP price, cash price, deposit, instalment details, dates, and regular collection.
Lease Agreement: Lessee gets right to use asset for rent; Lessor remains legal owner.

Finance Lease (AS-19): Transfers substantially all risks and rewards of ownership to lessee. Attributes: ownership transfers at end, purchase option below fair value, lease term for major economic life, present value of lease payments >= asset fair value, or specialized asset nature.
Operating Lease (AS-19): Lease other than finance lease; simple renting arrangement.

Accounting & Tax: Finance Lease -> Treated like loan; asset on lessee balance sheet; lessee claims interest & depreciation. Operating Lease -> Rent expense; lease payments charged to P&L; lessor claims depreciation.

flow.title: Lease Classification Test (AS-19)
steps: Does title transfer at end of lease?
Is there a bargain purchase option?
Is lease term >= major part (75%) of asset life?
Is PV of minimum lease payments >= substantially all fair value?
If YES to any -> Finance Lease (Loan treatment, Lessee takes Dep/Interest)
If NO to all -> Operating Lease (Rent treatment, Lessor takes Dep)

topics.example: A company leases a custom specialized machine for 8 years (its entire economic life). Since it spans the economic life and is specialized, AS-19 classifies it as a Finance Lease.
remember: In Hire Purchase, ownership passes on payment of the LAST instalment.
Finance Lease transfers substantially all risks and rewards; Operating Lease does not.
mistakes: Assuming a lessee in an Operating Lease can claim depreciation; depreciation can only be claimed by the lessor in an operating lease.

quiz.q: Under a Hire Purchase agreement, at what point does legal ownership of the goods pass to the hirer?
o: Upon signing the agreement
Upon delivery of the goods
Upon payment of the first instalment
Upon payment of the last instalment
quiz.why: In hire purchase, property/ownership passes only when the final instalment is fully paid.

quiz.q: Which accounting treatment applies to the lessee in an Operating Lease under AS-19?
o: Show asset in Balance Sheet and claim depreciation
Treat lease payments as operating rent expense in Profit & Loss
Capitalize all future lease payments as equity
Claim both interest and depreciation expenses
quiz.why: Operating leases are treated as rental arrangements; lease payments are expensed in P&L.

topics.title: Audit of Co-operative Societies (Central Act 1912)
explain: Appointment & Qualifications: Auditor appointed by Registrar of Co-operative Societies; can be a CA or holder of Govt diploma in co-operative accounts / former co-operative department auditor.
Sec 17 Audit: Mandates annual audit by Registrar/authorized person; includes examining overdue debts and asset/liability valuation.
Sec 5 Shareholding Limit: In limited liability society, no individual member (except a registered society) can hold > 20% of total shares OR share value > ₹1,000.
Sec 29 & 30 Restrictions: Cannot lend to non-members without Registrar sanction; borrowing subject to bye-laws.
Sec 32 Investments: Central/State Co-op Bank, Trust Act Sec 20 securities, shares of other limited co-op societies.
Sec 33 & 34 Profits: Transferred to Reserve Fund before dividend; max 10% of remaining net profit can be donated to charitable purposes after compulsory reserve transfer.

Special Features: Classify overdue debts (6m to 5yr, >5yr); exclude overdue interest from profit (credit to Reserve); Bad debts written off ONLY when certified by auditor (e.g. Maharashtra rules); pass profit appropriations ONLY AFTER General Body approval.

flow.title: Co-operative Profit Allocation Sequence
steps: Calculate Net Profit for the financial year
Deduct Education Fund contribution (charge on profit)
Transfer prescribed statutory percentage to Reserve Fund (Sec 33)
Max 10% of remaining net profit to Charitable Purposes (Sec 34 with Registrar sanction)
General Body approves remaining appropriations/dividends
Pass accounting entries AFTER General Body approval date

topics.example: A co-op society has ₹10,000 net profit. It first transfers 25% to Reserve Fund (₹2,500). Out of the remaining ₹7,500, it can contribute a maximum of 10% (₹750) to charity with Registrar approval.
remember: Individual shareholding limit: Max 20% of total shares OR ₹1,000 in value (Sec 5).
Charitable contribution limit: Max 10% of net profit remaining after compulsory Reserve Fund transfer (Sec 34).
Bad debts require auditor certification before write-off under state rules like Maharashtra.
mistakes: Passing proposed profit appropriation entries before General Body approval; in co-op accounting, entries are passed ONLY AFTER General Body approval.

quiz.q: Under Section 5 of the Co-operative Societies Act, 1912, what is the maximum shareholding value an individual member can hold in a limited liability society?
quiz.why: Section 5 limits individual shareholding to a maximum of 20% of total shares or ₹1,000 in share value.

quiz.q: How does co-operative society accounting differ from corporate accounting regarding profit appropriations?
o: Corporate accounting passes entries after AGM; Co-ops pass entries before AGM
Co-operative accounting entries for profit appropriation are passed ONLY AFTER General Body approval
Co-operative societies never transfer profits to reserve funds
Co-operative societies cannot distribute dividends
quiz.why: Unlike companies which record proposed dividends, co-op accounting entries are made post-General Body approval.

topics.title: Multi-State Co-operative Societies (Act 2002)
explain: Applies to co-op societies operating in more than one state. Political donations are strictly prohibited.
Sec 72 Auditor Qualification: ONLY a Chartered Accountant can be appointed. Disqualified: Body corporate, officer/employee, partner/employee of officer/employee, person indebted > ₹1,000.
Sec 70 Appointment: 1st auditor appointed by Board within 1 month of registration; subsequent auditors appointed at each AGM.
Sec 73 Auditor Duties: Right of access to books; inquiries on secured loans, book entry transactions, personal expenses charged to revenue, cash for share allotment.

Sec 77 Special Audit: Central Govt can order Special Audit if society managed against co-op principles, causing injury to trade, or solvency endangered; ONLY IF Govt holds >= 51% paid-up share capital.
Sec 78 Inquiry & Sec 79 Inspection: Central Registrar can initiate inquiry/inspection on request of federal co-op, creditor, 1/3rd board, or 1/5th members; requires 15 days prior notice.

flow.title: Special Audit & Inquiry Triggers (Act 2002)
steps: Check multi-state status & Govt shareholding (Must be >= 51% for Sec 77)
Identify trigger: Non-prudent management / Injury to trade / Solvency danger
Central Govt issues Special Audit Order u/s 77
Special Auditor submits report to Central Govt (not members)
For Sec 78/79 Inquiry/Inspection: Issue 15 days prior notice
Central Registrar communicates report within 3 months

topics.example: Central Govt holds 60% share capital in a multi-state agri-export co-op. Following complaints of fund diversion endangering solvency, Central Govt invokes Sec 77 to appoint a CA for Special Audit.
remember: Special Audit u/s 77 requires Govt shareholding of AT LEAST 51%.
Inquiry (Sec 78) & Inspection (Sec 79) require at least 15 days prior notice.
Indebtedness disqualification limit for auditor: > ₹1,000.
mistakes: Believing non-CAs can audit Multi-State Co-op Societies; ONLY Chartered Accountants are qualified u/s 72.

quiz.q: What minimum Government shareholding is required for the Central Government to direct a Special Audit u/s 77 of the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002?
quiz.why: Central Govt can order a special audit under Section 77 only if Govt holds 51% or more paid-up share capital.

quiz.q: Prior notice of how many days must be given to a Multi-State Co-operative Society before holding an inquiry u/s 78 or inspection u/s 79?
o: 7 days
15 days
30 days
60 days
quiz.why: Sections 78 and 79 require a mandatory minimum 15 days prior written notice before conducting inquiry/inspection.

topics.title: Audit of Trusts & Societies
topics.section: Societies Registration Act 1860 / Indian Trusts Act 1882 / Income Tax Act 1961
explain: Legal forms: Public Trusts (governed by State Public Trust Acts or Indian Trusts Act 1882), Societies (Societies Registration Act 1860), and Section 8 Companies.
Mandatory Books of Account: Cash book, ledger, journal, serially-numbered bill copies & receipt counterfoils, original voucher bills, and state-prescribed registers.
Auditor Working Papers must document: work done & by whom, explanations given & by whom, decisions taken, judicial pronouncements relied upon, and client certificates.
Working paper evidence must prove audit opinion is based on examination, not arbitrary, and supported by full information tested for accuracy.

Trust Audit Checks: Verify accounts regularity, donations applied as per objects/donor directions, cash balance agreement, property register updates, trustee count, minute books, and cash donation limits.
Society Audit Checks: Verify governing legislation, Memorandum objects, FCRA registration, Income Tax 12A/80G status, accounting for reimbursed expenses, and Registrar inquiries.

flow.title: Trust Audit Verification Workflow
steps: Obtain mandatory list of books of accounts maintained
Examine Trust Deed / Memorandum of Association
Physical verification of cash balance & property register
Check donations applied strictly as per trust objects
Verify trustee count, meeting minutes & interest in investments
Maintain detailed audit working papers & issue report

topics.example: During a trust audit, the auditor checks the Property Register, physically inspects title deeds of land owned by the trust, and ensures cash donations do not exceed prescribed income tax limits.
remember: Auditors of trusts/societies must comply with mandatory Accounting Standards (AS) and Standards on Auditing (SA).
Working papers must provide evidence that information obtained was subjected to test checks.
mistakes: Relying solely on management representations without performing independent verification of property records or donor receipts.

quiz.q: Which of the following must be documented in audit working papers for a Trust audit?
o: Work done and by whom
Explanations received and by whom
Judicial pronouncements relied upon
All of the above
quiz.why: Working papers must contain notes on work done, explanations received, decisions, legal cases relied upon, and certificates.

quiz.q: If a trust receives a donation with a specific direction from the donor, how must the auditor verify its application?
o: Ensure it is credited to the local municipality
Verify it is applied strictly in accordance with the donor's specific direction and trust objects
Ensure it is distributed to trustees as remuneration
Transfer it to political election funds
quiz.why: Specific direction donations must be utilized strictly as instructed by the donor aligned with trust objects.
